evidence.description: C1 TTS fallback ladder + 'do NOT dial' silent-call guard enumerated
C2 mixed/unresolvable endpoint -> whole-request Google fallback; 0 journeys/non-200/timeout -> Google fallback, logged
C3 TTL + time-bucket sizing explicitly required to force recompute on a moved event
C4 partial-grant edge (calendar but not gmail) requires onboarding to reflect true state
C5 debounce (>=2 consecutive FAILs), rollback-target-must-itself-pass flap guard, one-message-per-incident Telegram dedup
C7 NO-OP-is-valid edge when leading signal is absent

supaUsers (batch) and getUserByUid (per-uid refetch) confirmed as two distinct hardcoded calendar_provider=eq.composio_gcal call sites, consistently reproduced across both scheduler.js copies inspected -- matches C4's 'BOTH selector sites' framing (FIND-003 iter-2, now resolved)
claimTravel/unclaimTravel confirm lm_travel_log stays a pure {uid,event_key,leg} dedup ledger, distinct from the new lm_route_cache C3 proposes -- no structural conflation
mail-unipile.js / mail-gog.js kept behind a single transport interface (send/listInbox) -- clean module boundary, no duplication introduced by this spec's proposed changes

priorFindingsNotes.FIND-001: iter-2 FIND-001 (false 'reply-by-email, never read Gmail' claim) is technically corrected in spec text (C4 line 77 now says Gmail-READ stays on the existing provider for EMAIL users), BUT this corrected claim is itself now contradicted by the actual ask.js on disk in the lipsync-monk worktree, which has moved to a Resend-inbound-webhook mechanism that explicitly never reads Gmail -- while a second worktree (agent-a6417f77d0f47a1cc) still has the old Gmail-read-via-Unipile ask.js the spec describes. Reopened as iteration-3 FIND-001.
priorFindingsNotes.FIND-002: Same root cause as FIND-001 above -- the Pipedream gmail.send-only regression concern (iter-2 FIND-002) is reframed around a Gmail-read mechanism that appears to already be obsolete in at least one code branch (Resend-inbound webhook, not Gmail polling), so the spec's current mitigation may be answering the wrong current-state question. Reopened as iteration-3 FIND-001.
priorFindingsNotes.FIND-003: iter-2 FIND-003 (only scheduler.js:42 widened, getUserByUid:271 not mentioned) is now resolved in spec text (C4 line 78 names BOTH sites) and confirmed structurally consistent across both available scheduler.js copies. Resolved.
priorFindingsNotes.FIND-004: iter-2 FIND-004 (Stripe-link extraction method internally contradictory) is resolved: C5 CHECK(b) (line 85) now correctly describes a bundle/chunk-string extraction, and LmClient.tsx:34,453-455 on disk confirms STRIPE_LM_URL is a module-level constant that will be present in the /lm route's compiled JS chunk regardless of the ?tg= gate (LmBody.tsx statically imports LmClient). Resolved.
priorFindingsNotes.FIND-005: iter-2 FIND-005 (branch ambiguity) is nominally addressed by pinning CANONICAL=origin/main (spec line 8), but the practical problem recurs in a new form: neither the adversary's toolset nor the repo's checked-out state can reach origin/main (see iteration-3 FIND-004), and the available worktrees actively disagree with each other and with the spec's own attributions (see iteration-3 FIND-001/FIND-002). Partially resolved -- the DECLARATION of a canonical branch does not by itself make disk-facts checkable or true.
priorFindingsNotes.FIND-006: iter-2 FIND-006 (wake schedule table dropped T-15) is NOT resolved -- reopened with a worse defect: the spec's specific claim about WHICH worktree holds the stale 3-level variant (line 25: 'the 3-level T-15 variant exists only in the stale lipsync-monk worktree') is factually backwards versus observed disk state (lipsync-monk currently has the 2-level version; agent-a6417f77d0f47a1cc has the 3-level version). See iteration-3 FIND-002.
priorFindingsNotes.FIND-007: iter-2 FIND-007 (circular JP gate / unproven address->geo) is conceptually redesigned (C2 line 64: single places/suggest call resolves geo AND probes JP-resolvability, removing the sequencing circularity) but remains EMPIRICALLY unverified: no fixture demonstrates places/suggest geocoding a real postal address (only pre-resolved geo: inputs are fixture-tested), and §4's RED plan has no test for this mechanism. See iteration-3 FIND-003.

convergenceSignals.note: All iteration-1 blockers remain resolved. Of iteration-2's 7 findings, FIND-003 and FIND-004 are now genuinely resolved (verified against available disk copies). FIND-005 is only partially resolved (declaring 'origin/main is canonical' does not make it checkable). FIND-006 is reopened with a factually backwards worktree attribution. FIND-007 is only partially resolved (sound redesign, zero empirical evidence). FIND-001/FIND-002's underlying Gmail-read claim is reopened because the corrected spec text is itself contradicted by at least one current ask.js implementation. A structural blocker underlies all of this: this review could not reach the spec's declared canonical source (origin/main) with the tools and repository state available, so several 're-verified 2026-07-03' claims in the spec are unconfirmed or actively contradicted by the best available evidence. Overall FAIL: 4 major findings, 2 of 5 dimensions FAIL.
